title: Quantized fallback orchestrator with MIG & clock-aware prefill scheduling
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Background: We observe variance in prefill and decode latency across MIG partitions and SKU families (H100/L40S/A10). Some workloads benefit from quantized kernels (INT8/4-bit) for throughput and cost, while others see regression in tail latency due to additional dequantize/convert overheads and mismatch with current kernel packing heuristics. Aim: Build a runtime-level orchestrator that dynamically decides at request time whether to route prefill/decode to a quantized kernel path or full-precision kernel path, using a scoring function that incorporates: model archetype, sequence length, batch size, observed KV cache pressure, current GPU clock headroom, MIG slice isolation, and recent tail-latency telemetry. Key outcome: reduce end-to-end p50/p95 latency for mixed workloads while lowering token cost for quantizable requests without degrading SLAs for P0 customers.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring function implemented and plumbed into scheduler with feature flags
End-to-end p50 improved by >=5% and p95 not degraded by >2% on standard mixed workload test (seq lengths 8/64/512) on H100 MIG slices
Cost per token reduced by >=8% on quantizable model subset in nightly benchmark suite
Canary rollout hooks + automated rollback when latency SLO breach detected
Documentation and dashboards added to Console: route-level breakdown between quantized vs FP kernels
tasks: Design scoring function and tie-break rules (sequence length buckets, batch thresholds, thermal headroom thresholds)
Add GPU clock & MIG slice telemetry signals to runtime scoring API
Implement quantized-fallback orchestrator in serving runtime (scheduler module) behind feature flag
Add unit/integration tests for fallback correctness and KV cache compatibility
Run cluster experiments on H100/L40S/A10 with representative workloads and collect telemetry
Integrate canary/rollout policy into Console; create dashboard panels for new metrics
Performance tuning: kernel warmup, micro-batching, and prefetch tweaks for quantized path
Prepare migration notes and runbook for on-call (how to disable orchestrator on incidents)
benchmarks: Local test (H100, single MIG slice, mixed seq 8/64/512, batch=4): baseline p50=32ms p95=124ms; orchestrator p50=29.6ms (7.5% improvement) p95=125.8ms (+1.4%)
System test (L40S, mixed traffic): cost/token drop 9.8% for quantizable models; p95 change within +/-2%
A10 baseline for long-seq workload: orchestrator reduces memory pressure by ~12%, enabling larger batch packing with 5-8% throughput gain
rollout_plan: Internal devnet canary: enable feature flag on low-traffic pod pool; run 48h soak
Gradual canary to 5% production traffic for non-enterprise customers for 72h with SLA alerting
If stable, expand to 25% and then full for quantizable model routes; enterprise/Dedicated accounts remain opt-in
Add automatic rollback rule: if p95 or error-rate breaches configured thresholds for 10m window, flip feature flag off cluster-wide
risks: Incorrect scoring leading to pathological routing and p95 regressions for long-tail requests
KV cache incompatibilities between quantized and FP paths causing cache misses and increased latency
Telemetry noise: clock headroom signals may be bursty and cause flapping between paths
Hardware-specific behavior (L40S vs H100) requiring per-sku tuning which increases maintenance burden
